citations.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent.

readings.distinction: On the broader entity-level parse, the final qualification restricts the entire applicability proposition for both LC-held and AE-held money. Negation attaches to the LC’s acting as a Transfer Agent. Concurrent transfer-agent work can therefore defeat the selected antecedent even where the particular money is handled in another capacity.

citations.quote: Would activities that an RA 13 depositary performs in its capacity as a Transfer Agent (TA) (eg, processing payments in designated accounts) be subject to requirements under the CMR?
only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent

In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).

readings.distinction: On the activity-specific parse, the final qualification still restricts the whole applicability proposition, but “acting” concerns the capacity in which the particular funds are handled. This reading is contextually preferred because Q1 expressly asks about activities performed in a transfer-agent capacity. The answer’s unqualified reference to “such LC” leaves the broader reading defensible.

The vocabulary does not distinguish LC-held money from AE-held money or separately identify the AE’s capacity. The target expressly tests the role of “such LC”.

There is no input for Schedule 11 duties or their particular conditions. Q1’s “In such cases” follows its discussion of non-scheme money; continuing duties cannot be encoded as a universal consequence of a false Q1 predicate.
